title: Resolve invoice rounding + rate-limit refund allocation causing NetSuite export variance
creator: Aisha Kumar
description: Background: Over the last quarter we've seen ~0.8% of invoices exported to NetSuite have dollar-level variance vs Stripe and internal ledger. Root cause analysis points to two interacting issues: (1) rate-limit refund credits were created as fractional token-credit amounts but then rounded differently in the nightly billing export job, and (2) the NetSuite mapping assumes invoice lines sum to the Stripe gross/total and applies NetSuite rounding rules again, amplifying small per-line truncation errors into visible invoice mismatches. This ticket consolidates fixes for the export pipeline, adds a deterministic rounding/aggregation strategy, and includes a backfill job to align historical exports for the last 90 days.
acceptance_criteria: Nightly billing_export job emits per-invoice CSV where sum(line_amounts) == invoice_total for 100k-sample (no variance > $0.01)
Stripe reconcile job shows zero unexplained mismatch for invoices processed after rollout in staging and canary
NetSuite import mapping accepts the new export without throwing 'line-sum mismatch' warnings for canary tenants
Backfill job corrects historical NetSuite attachments for 30/90 day windows and logs changes (audit-friendly)
Unit & integration tests cover rate-limit credit edge cases (fractional credits, negative adjustments, multiple refunds across cycle)
tasks: Audit existing billing_export aggregation code (jobs/billing/exporter.py) and capture current rounding behavior
Implement deterministic aggregation: compute all line-level fractional cents in high-precision (millicents), defer rounding to invoice-level using round-half-to-even
Ensure rate-limit credits/refunds are represented as separate adjustment lines with explicit 'credit_type' and original usage reference
Update NetSuite export mapper to use exported invoice_total instead of recomputing lines; add protective validation and soft-fail mode
Add migration/backfill job to regenerate exports for last 90 days and push corrected CSVs to s3://redwood-billing/backfills/ and NetSuite staging
Add unit tests + e2e test harness using stripe-testdata fixture and a mini-netsuite-mock
Canary rollout to 5 high-volume customers, monitor for anomalies for 72 hours, then full rollout

sql_queries:
-- Repro query: invoices where exported_total != computed_total
SELECT invoice_id, exported_total, SUM(line_amount) as computed_total, exported_total - SUM(line_amount) as diff_cents
FROM billing.invoice_lines l JOIN billing.exports e ON l.invoice_id = e.invoice_id
WHERE e.export_date >= '2025-01-01'
GROUP BY invoice_id, exported_total
HAVING ABS(exported_total - SUM(line_amount)) > 0.01;

-- Identify fractional credit patterns
SELECT invoice_id, COUNT(*) as credit_lines, SUM(line_amount) as credit_total
FROM billing.invoice_lines
WHERE credit_type = 'rate_limit_refund'
GROUP BY invoice_id
HAVING SUM(line_amount) != ROUND(SUM(line_amount), 2);
rollout_plan: 1) Merge PR with feature flag 'billing_export_rounding_v2' off; 2) Ship to staging + run full integration against stripe-testdata and netsuite-mock; 3) Turn feature flag on for canary orgs (5 orgs) and run backfill for those orgs to NetSuite staging; 4) Monitor metrics for 72 hours (mismatch-rate, export-errors, net-suite-import-warnings); 5) If stable, enable for all orgs and execute 90-day backfill in throttled batches; 6) Post-rollout retrospective and finance sign-off to mark done.
monitoring: Dashboards: billing/mismatch-rate, billing/export-latency, netsuite/import-warnings. Alerts: mismatch-rate > 0.1% (P0), export job failure > 1 per hour (P1). Log sample retention for backfill runs: 365 days. Add structured audit events for any invoices changed by backfill (backfill_job_id, original_export_sha, corrected_export_sha).
